remarks: Per the spec, non-government aggregator/consultancy sources surfaced by WebSearch (e.g. indiafilings.com, wikiprocedure.com, prsindia.org, simpliance.in, compfie.aparajitha.com, employmentlaw.lkslaw.com, legalitysimplified.com, corpbiz.io, professionalutilities.com) were deliberately NOT curl-verified or included, even though some repeated useful facts (e.g. issuing authority, five-year validity, worker thresholds) — those facts conflicted across sources and are flagged here as unverified, not included as citations.

The 'Requirements' button for the Factory Licence service on https://eodb.arunachal.gov.in/active-services loads its checklist content via a JS modal (onclick=getRequirementDataFromModal(13)) that calls a backend endpoint; this could not be retrieved with a plain curl GET, so the detailed document checklist for Arunachal Pradesh's Factory Licence specifically could not be independently verified this session beyond what the Active Services page itself states.

The verified fee-schedule PDF is a scanned page from the Arunachal Pradesh Extraordinary Gazette of March 6, 2012 (the original Factories Rules, 2012 notification), which confirms the regulatory basis for the fee tables; however, a complete, independently-verified consolidated text of the Arunachal Pradesh Factories Rules, 2012 (or any later Factories Amendment Rules, 2025 draft) hosted on a reachable .gov.in domain was not found this session — candidates for it (compfie.aparajitha.com, simpliance.in) are non-government mirrors and were excluded per the spec's aggregator rule rather than curl-checked.

indarun.gov.in's doing-business checklist page (htm/doingbusiness.htm) was fetched and inspected (HTTP 200, real content) but is a general MSME/NOC setup checklist that does not name 'Factory License' specifically, so it was left out of verifiedSources/excluded as not clearly on-topic rather than as a verification failure.

www.nsws.gov.in was verified only as the general central homepage; no Arunachal-Pradesh- or factory-license-specific NSWS sub-page could be located and confirmed this session (the site is heavily JavaScript/API-driven beyond the landing page).
